title.analysis: Authentic title "You'll Stop Working BEFORE 50 Once You Understand This" is a curiosity-gap promise with an age anchor. The script delivers the anchor (one number: savings rate) within the first minute and the title promise is honoured, with an explicit late caveat that a 50% savings rate is far easier at high incomes. The "before 50" framing rests on the savings-rate table, which assumes a 5% real return and the 4% rule the video later says is too generous.

script.opening_words: Here's a sentence that shouldn't make sense. The highest earner in your office will probably never retire and one of the lowest earners might be done by 45. Same building, same years, opposite endings. Take Robert. Right now, on a random Tuesday, he's making coffee in his sweatpants. 47, no alarm, no commute, never going back to work. Now, take Zoe, three desks down for two decades, who out-earned him every year. She's crawling through the same traffic she's sat
script.ending_words: You don't have to retire at 45. That was never really the point. The point is that the choice exists, the math is real, and the only thing standing between you and it is a percentage you actually control. Go figure out your number this week. And if you want a hand running it, you already know where to find me. I'm Nick. I'll see you in the next one.
script.analysis: Full 17767 canonical characters read. A single-narrator early-retirement explainer built around two composite coworkers (Robert, who saved ~half his pay, and Zoe, who out-earned him and spent it): hook, savings-rate table, double effect of spending less, 4% rule and a 2026 valuation caveat moving it to ~3.5%, three levers and lifestyle creep, account order, Munger compounding quote, early-access paths (Roth ladder, 72(t), Roth contributions), ACA subsidy strategy with a 2026 caveat, Robert's compounding inflection, a school-community promotion, and an honest income caveat. Arithmetic is internally consistent; main errors are the incomplete 72(t) rule and the loose 3.5%/30x pairing.
beat_map: Hook: highest earner never retires, Robert vs Zoe.
Savings rate as the one number; 10% to 75% table.
Double lever of spending less; $60,000 example; $500,000 earner at zero.
Three levers; lifestyle creep and hedonic adaptation.
Account order: 401(k) match, HSA, IRA, brokerage.
Early access: Roth ladder, 72(t), Roth contributions.
Health insurance before 65; income-based subsidies; 2026 caveat.
Honest catch: income matters; 10% to 20% saves ~14 years; close.
